To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UFMC is the best choice for 5G, when transmitting very short packets, due to its high spectral efficiency, low latency and robustness to inter-symbol interference.
FBMC is the most efficient waveform for the transmission of long sequences while UFMC performs best for the transmission of short packets.
FBMC is the most efficient waveform for long packets, OFDM is the least efficient, and that UFMC is the most suitable waveform for short packet transmissions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of different waveforms for short packet and low latency transmission.
the design, performance and implementation of advanced communication schemes.
the suitability of different waveform contenders for the air interface design of 5G.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UFMC is a promising candidate to be considered for future wireless systems.
UFMC is the best choice for 5G, but it depends on the application and the requirements.
OFDM should be avoided in any case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UFMC outperforms OFDM and FBMC in the short packet regime, but that the latter performs better in the long packet regime.
FBMC is the best choice for long packets, UFMC for short packets and OFDM for long packets under very tight latency requirements.
FBMC is the best choice for long packets and low latency, OFDM for long packets and high latency, and UFMC for short packets and low latency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of waveform is very important in the context of short packet and/or low latency transmissions, and that UFMC should be seriously considered in the context of 5G.
the waveform choice for 5G is not a simple one and should not be based on the 4G choice of OFDM.
UFMC can be considered a serious contender for 5G.
